Simulation study comparing three BWQS specifications from `src/models.jl`:

* `bwqs` – flat Dirichlet prior on the weights;
* `bwqs_adv` – hierarchical Dirichlet (`alpha ~ Gamma(2, 2)`, the former `bwqs_new`);
* `bwqs_soft` – logit-Dirichlet prior (`DirichletLogit`).

It also shows how to run multiple chains in parallel with `Distributed`.

Sources: `met_classification/test_mixture.jl` (most recent version, kept as
the main simulation), the BWQS part of `met_classification/bayesian_stuff.jl`
and `met_classification/multichain_test.jl`.

```{julia}
using ExposomicsJulia
using LinearAlgebra, Distributions, Statistics, StatsBase, Random
using Turing, ReverseDiff, CSV, DataFrames
DATA = joinpath(pkgdir(ExposomicsJulia), ".data")
```

## Simulated mixture

55 mixture components, 2 covariates, weights drawn from a flat Dirichlet.

```{julia}
rng = MersenneTwister(1990);
N  = 342
XM = rand(rng, Normal(0.0, 0.2), N, 55)
XC = rand(rng, Normal(0.0, 0.2), N, 2)
w  = rand(rng, Dirichlet(ones(55)))
a, b = 1.1, -0.23
d  = [1.1, -0.12]

ecdf_score!(XM; scale = 4)

mmix = a .+ b * (XM * w) .+ XC * d
y = rand(rng, MvNormal(mmix, 0.85 * I));
```

```{julia}
#| eval: false
sampler = NUTS(; adtype = AutoReverseDiff(; compile = true))
m_soft  = bwqs_soft(XC, XM, y; alpha = fill(50.0, size(XM, 2)), phi = 10.0)  # fixed-prior version
m_adv   = bwqs_adv(XC, XM, y; alpha_prior = Gamma(2.0, 2.0))
m_flat  = bwqs(XC, XM, y)
chain_soft = sample(m_soft, sampler, 1000)
chain_adv  = sample(m_adv,  sampler, 1000)
chain_flat = sample(m_flat, sampler, 1000)
chain_summary(chain_soft; pattern = "w[")
```

Compare the estimated weights with the truth:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
DataFrame(true_w = w,
          soft = posterior_mean(chain_soft, :w),
          adv  = posterior_mean(chain_adv, :w),
          flat = posterior_mean(chain_flat, :w))
```

## Small mixture with learned logit-Dirichlet prior

Five components with known weights; here `bwqs_soft` learns `alpha` and
`phi` (version from `bayesian_stuff.jl`).

```{julia}
XM5 = rand(Normal(0.0, 0.2), 200, 5)
XC5 = rand(Normal(0.0, 0.2), 200, 2)
w5  = [0.5, 0.2, 0.2, 0.05, 0.05]
ecdf_score!(XM5; scale = 4)
y5  = rand(MvNormal(1.1 .+ -0.23 * (XM5 * w5) .+ XC5 * [1.1, -0.12], 0.85 * I));
```

```{julia}
#| eval: false
sampler = NUTS(; adtype = AutoReverseDiff(; compile = true))
chain_soft5 = sample(bwqs_soft(XC5, XM5, y5), sampler, 1000)
chain_flat5 = sample(bwqs(XC5, XM5, y5), sampler, 5000)
chain_summary(chain_flat5; pattern = "w[")
```

The scripts also fitted the same models to a small example dataset
(`bwqs_tmp.csv`: columns 2–6 mixture, 7–9 covariates, `y` outcome),
originally at `https://envbran.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/bwqs_tmp.csv`
(no longer publicly reachable) or `C:/Users/nicol/Documents/bwqs_tmp.csv`;
put a copy in `.data/bwqs_tmp.csv`.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
DT = CSV.read(joinpath(DATA, "bwqs_tmp.csv"), DataFrame)
XMd = Matrix(DT[:, 2:6]); XCd = Matrix(DT[:, 7:9]); yd = DT[:, :y]
chain_tmp = sample(bwqs(XCd, XMd, yd), NUTS(), MCMCThreads(), 5000, 4)
```

## Multiple chains on several processes

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Distributed
addprocs(4; exeflags = "--project=$(Base.active_project())")
@everywhere using ExposomicsJulia, Turing, CSV, DataFrames

@everywhere begin
    DT = CSV.read(joinpath(DATA, "bwqs_tmp.csv"), DataFrame)
    model_bwqs_multi = bwqs_adv(Matrix(DT[:, 7:9]), Matrix(DT[:, 2:6]), DT[:, :y];
                                alpha_prior = Gamma(2.0, 2.0))
end

chain_multi = sample(model_bwqs_multi, NUTS(), MCMCDistributed(), 50_000, 4)
```

Open points noted in the original scripts: a Student-t BWQS to account for
outliers and heavy tails, spatial models, and computational stability of the
mixture model.
